charter:
# Charter — T19F Decision-Forum Governance (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

- **Project:** T19F 'Decision-forum governance (follow-on)', track v2, ADM phase G, capability
  plateau, tranche 6, plan `docs/plans/T19F-meeting-bindings.md`, issues #682 (plan), #683
  (implementation) and #684 (live proof).
- **Sponsor:** the programme's sponsoring group, through the tranche-6 PI plan and the standing
  delegation `01a1fb9f-ac2d-732d-b274-1079be3dd2b3`.
- **Authority:** SPEC V2 D66 and the T19 decision-forum model. T19 made the meeting the decision
  forum; T19F closes the two seams T19 left: a forum policy could only be created implicitly and
  never changed, and the T9 body and T10 cadence resolved a meeting only by convention.
- **Objective:** a policy change is authored through the tenant's authoring route and published as
  a new immutable `meeting_type` version while an in-flight meeting keeps its pinned version; a
  board subject decision is taken in a board sitting, with one `approval_decision` row per
  qualifying seat carrying `via='meeting'`; a cadence row names its meeting type and materialises
  exactly one meeting; the direct `architecture.board_decide` path is unchanged.
- **Scope in:** migration `0073_meeting_bindings.sql`, the `authoring.publish` hook, the
  `meetings.type_list`/`type_get` reads, `architecture.board_sit_open`/`board_sit_decide`,
  `cadences.materialise`, the mock and real meetings surfaces, the MSP/TOGAF/SAFe artefact set and
  the live gate.
- **Scope out:** a second decision store; a chat, AV or transcript store; a rebuild of T9's board,
  T10's cadence or the approval primitive; any change to the direct `board_decide` path; the T18
  shell/nav; and any LLM that selects agenda items, positions or attendance.
- **Constraints:** `meeting_type` rows stay immutable and a meeting pins its version; a reused
  authoring asset key is refused, so a new version needs a new key; `cadences.materialise` locks the
  cadence row before the existing-instance lookup, because T19's `uq_meeting_live` already owns the
  slot rule; no new table and no FK on a versioned key.
- **Closure status:** T19F remains `active`. The plan's §10 records that the closure review accepts
  the delivered scope and defers closure to the tranche-6 review; this pack therefore carries no
  closure keys, and the live gate (13/13 at 2026-11-27T00:10Z) is the project's proof.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — T19F Decision-Forum Governance (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

body.assignment: The architecture work assigns T19F the binding layer between the programme's decision forums and the governance records: a versioned authoring route for forum policy, an explicit meeting-type binding on the governance body and the programme cadence, and the board-sitting action that decides through T19's own arithmetic. This statement governs the retrospective record of work delivered in #682–#684 and re-read at the 2026-11-27 snapshot.
body.scope: In scope are `migrations/0073_meeting_bindings.sql` (additive columns and one partial unique index), the `authoring.publish` hook that writes the next `meeting_type` version for a reviewed `kind='policy'` asset, `meetings.type_list` and `meetings.type_get`, `architecture.board_sit_open` and `board_sit_decide`, `cadences.materialise`, the meetings surfaces in the design mock and the real app, and the live gate. Out of scope is any second decision store or any rebuild of T9, T10 or the approval primitive.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors this retrospective statement; the delivery team (conveyor-e2e) is accountable for the evidence; the Architecture Board is both the reviewer of the artefact set and, through its own sitting, the deciding forum the capability serves; the SRO accepts the deferred closure at the tranche-6 review. T19 and T17 are consulted as the reused primitives.
body.acceptance_criteria: The live gate is the acceptance: a policy v2 published through the authoring route while the pinned meeting still resolves v1; a board sitting whose approval carries one per-seat decision with `via.surface='meeting'` and a chair attribution; a cadence materialised twice yielding exactly one non-cancelled meeting bound to the cadence's type; and the direct board path still recording. The evidence is `docs/evidence/t19f/live-gate-check.txt` (13/13 PASS) and the state in `docs/evidence/t19f/live-gate.json`.
body.constraints: The policy model is a versioned release, not an edit: a published asset key cannot be reused and a meeting never follows a later version. The cadence materialisation takes a row lock before the lookup so the one-instance promise does not silently become a stronger scheduling rule than T19's `uq_meeting_live`. The direct `architecture.board_decide` path is deliberately untouched, so a body without a sitting behaves exactly as before.
body.retrospective: This statement of architecture work is authored on 2026-11-27 for the tranche-6 rework. The plan, the implementation and the live proof were delivered through #682–#684, and the artefact set in `docs/plans/T19F/` is the contemporaneous documentation. The statement adds the MSP/TOGAF lifecycle framing the retrospective requires and records the deferred closure explicitly.

# Architecture Artefact Index — T19F (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

## Metadata

The artefact set for T19F is the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts on the delivery track: the Stakeholder Map, Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog, Requirements Catalog and Solution Concept Diagram at phase a, plateau psa; the Business Capability Map at phase b; the Data Entity/Data Component Catalog at phase c; and the Technology Standards Catalog at phase d. Each carries an authored body dated 2026-11-27; the owner is the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation, the reviewer is the Architecture Board, and the subject is this project's record.

## Entries

The set is seven rows in the order the standard seeds them: a/matrix — Stakeholder Map — T19F Decision-Forum Governance (Phase A); a/catalog — Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog — T19F Decision-Forum Governance (Phase A); a/catalog — Requirements Catalog — T19F Decision-Forum Governance (Phase A); a/diagram — Solution Concept Diagram — T19F Decision-Forum Governance (Phase A); b/diagram — Business Capability Map — T19F Decision-Forum Governance (Phase B); c/catalog — Data Entity/Data Component Catalog — T19F Decision-Forum Governance (Phase C); d/catalog — Technology Standards Catalog — T19F Decision-Forum Governance (Phase D).

## Links

Every artefact links to another artefact of the set with one of the four §8.1 kinds. The links follow the phase order, so a reader can walk A to D without an orphan, and each artefact names its source in the plan (`docs/plans/T19F-meeting-bindings.md`) and in the tree (the migration, the store, the actions and the live gate).

## Document

This index is published as its own architecture-artifact document by the rework factory. It is the document the close gate reads for the project's artefact standard; it complements, rather than replaces, the contemporaneous MSP/TOGAF/SAFe documents under `docs/plans/T19F/` that the delivery produced.

risk.title: The live gate's approval lookup does not page, so a busy record can hide the sitting's row
risk.body: The gate resolves the sitting's approval through approvals.list. At the 2026-11-27T00:10Z run the row was on the first page; later the same day 592 approvals had been created after it and the un-paged lookup missed it, although the row is present and approved in the record. This unit fixes the instrument: read_approval pages approvals.list (limit 200, following next_cursor) until the row is found. The residual risk is the paging cap and a record that grows past it, which the instrument reports as an absent row rather than a pass.
risk.response: The paging fix lands in this unit and the gate re-runs green (13/13) at the fixed head; if the approval is ever reported absent again, check the page cap and the record identity before touching the assertion.

risk.title: The live gate depends on the record the transport reaches, not on a hermetic fixture
risk.body: The gate asserts rows on the programme record through the recorder's transport. A replayed or restored database carries the rows only if the gate's own apply run wrote them there; a fresh database would show them absent. The evidence file names the run and the state file names the ids, so the dependency is visible, but a future reader must not mistake the state file for a fixture.
risk.response: Record the record identity (replay container and database) alongside each gate run, and re-run --apply only when the record is intentionally rebuilt; never copy a state file across records.

issue.title: The record carried no lifecycle set for T19F; this pack supplies it retrospectively
issue.body: The plan (#682–#684) delivered the capability and its live proof, and the MSP/TOGAF/SAFe documents under docs/plans/T19F are contemporaneous. The programme record, however, carried no charter, baseline, contract, register set or Phase-G review for T19F. This pack adds that set at the 2026-11-27 snapshot without rewriting the delivery documents.
issue.response: This pack is the repair; the receipt at the pinned snapshot is the proof, and the tranche-6 review is the closure forum.

issue.title: Closure is deferred to the tranche-6 review by the plan's own §10
issue.body: The plan records that T19F remains active and that its closure review accepts the delivered scope and defers closure to the tranche-6 review. The project row is therefore active at this snapshot, and the pack carries no closure keys. The tranche-6 review is the decision that closes it.
issue.response: Close T19F in the tranche-6 review record and cite this deferral; do not close it in the rework factory, which would pre-empt the review.

assumption.title: The 2026-11-27 rework snapshot is the authoritative record for T19F
assumption.body: The delivery contract judges acceptance against the pinned snapshot; the checker refuses any id that appears nowhere in it. Every judgement in this pack is read from that snapshot, so if it is incomplete or stale for T19F the pack's facts and any re-close move with it.

assumption.title: The direct architecture.board_decide path stays unchanged
assumption.body: The plan's §4.4 records that the direct path, the approval primitive, T19's arithmetic, the minutes gate and the retirement flag are untouched. The assumption is that no later slice silently routes the direct path through a sitting; the suite `the_direct_board_decide_path_still_works` is the guard.

assumption.title: T19's uq_meeting_live remains the slot rule
assumption.body: The materialisation adds a cadence row lock rather than a stronger unique index, because T19's uq_meeting_live owns the slot rule and permits a second scheduled meeting. The assumption is that no migration later tightens that index without revisiting the materialisation contract.

dependency.title: T19F depends on T19 and T17 and on the tranche-5 authority
dependency.body: T19 supplies the meeting and the session as the decision forum and the outcome arithmetic; T17 supplies the versioned authoring route. The plan's §9 records these as provenance rather than a frozen order, and the tranche-5 review authorised tranche 6, which carries this project.

dependency.title: T19F is the last delivery member of tranche 6
dependency.body: The tranche-6 exit needs this project's receipt green; the tranche-6 review is the forum that closes it. Nothing after it in the tranche waits on its construction — the review waits on its receipt, which is the ordering the batch records.

benefit.title: Forum policy changes without mutating history
benefit.body: A policy change is a new immutable meeting_type version through the authoring route, and an in-flight meeting keeps the version it pinned. The benefit is an audit property: the policy a decision was taken under can be reconstructed from the meeting's pinned version, which the live gate asserts.

benefit.title: Board decisions are bound to the forum that took them
benefit.body: The sitting's approval carries one approval_decision per qualifying seat with via='meeting', so the decision can be traced to the forum and the chair seat rather than to an unbound board call. The benefit is declared in the plan and asserted by the sitting checks in the live gate.

benefit.title: One meeting per cadence slot, without a stronger scheduling contract
benefit.body: Materialising a cadence twice yields one non-cancelled meeting bound to the cadence's type and slot, and the row lock delivers the promise without changing T19's uq_meeting_live. The benefit is idempotence at the cadence boundary that the plan's P3 scenario records.

body.commitments: T19F delivers the two decision-forum bindings: a versioned policy authoring route through T17 that writes immutable meeting_type versions while meetings keep their pinned version, an explicit meeting-type binding on the governance body and the programme cadence, the board-sitting open/decide actions that decide through T19's arithmetic, and an idempotent cadence materialisation. The direct board path stays unchanged, and the project's closure is deferred to the tranche-6 review by its own plan.
body.compliance: Compliance is evidenced by `crates/api/tests/meetings_authoring.rs`, `crates/api/tests/meetings_binding.rs`, the design-pack checks and the live gate: `docs/evidence/t19f/live-gate-check.txt` records 13/13 PASS at 2026-11-27T00:10Z over the record, with the policy v1/v2, the sitting's per-seat decision and the cadence materialisation all asserted. The Phase-G review reads the same evidence at the pinned snapshot.
body.approval: The contract is approved by the board decision the factory records for this pack, under the standing delegation 01a1fb9f-ac2d-732d-b274-1079be3dd2b3; the Phase-G review is compliant for the record set, and the project stays active until the tranche-6 review takes the closure decision.

project_brief_output:
# Project Brief — T19F Decision-Forum Governance (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

## Outcome

A forum policy changes by publishing a new immutable version while an in-flight meeting keeps its pinned one; a board subject decision is taken in a sitting whose approval carries one decision per qualifying seat with `via='meeting'`; a cadence row names its meeting type and materialises exactly one meeting. The live gate asserts all three on the record, and the project's closure is deferred to the tranche-6 review.

## Boundary

T19F owns the policy authoring route, the body and cadence bindings, the sitting actions and the materialisation. It does not own the meeting arithmetic (T19), the authoring route itself (T17), the direct board path, the approval primitive, the T18 shell, or any chat/AV/transcript store. The `fr`-era decision surfaces are not revived.

## Reuse sources

T19's `close_item_tx` and the meeting outcome arithmetic; T17's `authoring.intake/draft/review/publish`; the existing approval and approval_decision rows; the existing `meeting`, `governance_body` and `programme_cadence` tables. The migration is additive and adds no table.

## Inception units

The plan's P1–P5 are the inception sequence: the policy authoring route and the type reads; the body-sitting binding; the cadence materialisation; the mock and real meetings surfaces; the programme record, the live chain and the live gate. Each has BDD scenarios with test targets in the plan.

## Dependencies

T19 supplies the decision forum and the arithmetic; T17 supplies the authoring route. The plan records #606/#650 as provenance, #655 as adjacent and #565/#566 as the T18 screen. The tranche-5 review authorised tranche 6, which carries this project as its last delivery member.

## Acceptance

The live gate is the acceptance: 13 checks over the policy v1/v2 pinning, the sitting's per-seat decision and the chair attribution, and the cadence materialisation, recorded in `docs/evidence/t19f/live-gate-check.txt`. The suites `meetings_authoring` and `meetings_binding` carry the construction proof, and the receipt is green on the sixteen manifest checks at the pinned snapshot.

## Capabilities

Versioned forum policy, bound board decisions, bound cadence slots and the preserved direct path. Each is delivered by a named action family and asserted by a suite or a live-gate check; the mechanisms are catalogued in the Phase C data view.

## Plan
